assessment: Banana appears in a list of potential dietary sources of trans-ferulic acid. The experiment administered purified trans-ferulic acid to mice and reported reduced locomotor activity and longer dark-compartment residence. It gives no raw banana exposure or Parkinson anxiety measure.

disposition: tarragon enjoyment reported during olfactory recovery
assessment: The case describes new enjoyment of tarragon odor and flavor during recovery from childhood anosmia after intranasal vitamin A and olfactory training. Tarragon enjoyment was a patient-reported outcome and the case does not estimate a dried tarragon treatment effect.

disposition: bell pepper recall without gait measurement
assessment: Red bell pepper contributed to estimated dietary polyphenols in the Chilean older-adult study. The authors explicitly excluded physical performance measures including gait speed and Timed Up and Go. There is no grilled bell pepper comparison.

disposition: isolated eugenol and open-arm behavior in mice
assessment: Commercial purified eugenol at 5 mg/kg increased open-arm time and entries on the elevated plus maze. The study examined isolated constituents in mice and provides no ground clove exposure or Parkinson anxiety outcome.

disposition: isolated capsiate and perceived exercise effort
assessment: The adult crossover used two 12 mg capsiate doses and compared ten-kilometer running and perceived exertion with placebo. The abstract reports an inconclusive RPE comparison (p=.517). Capsiate occurs in sweet pepper, and this experiment supplies no estimate for raw bell pepper or Parkinson fatigue.

disposition: isolated capsinoid and mechanistic pain context

assessment: The 2,451-participant cross-sectional study identified bell pepper as the usual sweet pepper. It measured timed four-meter walking within the composite, with no separate pepper-gait coefficient or grilled preparation. PMID33770761 is already assessed for this claim.

disposition: generic chili frequency and composite sarcopenia
assessment: Participants mainly reported finger-shaped chili. The questionnaire recorded chili intake frequency without a specific cayenne or ground preparation. Four-meter walk time helped define the composite outcome, and no separate chili and gait coefficient was reported.

assessment: The ACTIFOX crossover found no reported difference in perceived fatigue during 60 minutes of cycling after dihydrocapsiate in canola oil or cellulose placebo. Rating data were not shown. PMID35875695 is already assessed for this claim.

assessment: The introduction attributes pain and gastrointestinal symptoms after high-dose capsaicin to earlier work. The current crossover used purified dihydrocapsiate during aerobic exercise and did not test ground cayenne or measure clinical pain.

disposition: unmatched canola carrier and exercise fatigue
assessment: Canola oil of unspecified grade carried purified dihydrocapsiate. Control capsules used cellulose and the crossover reported no perceived-fatigue difference. Both the active constituent and carrier differed across arms, so the oil effect cannot be isolated.
